items.q: What should you remember about **Market vs maturity**?
items.a: **Mate-value "market forces" dominate brief first** meetings; repeated exposure reduces the advantage of universally desirable people and enables idiosyncratic matches.

items.q: What should you remember about **Apps ≠ real life**?
items.a: **Swipe markets are among the most unequal;** they turn dating into trait-impression interviews and favor hyperverbal texters over good in-person listeners.

items.q: What should you remember about **Slow spark is normal**?
items.a: **Most relationships start with middling first impressions,** not instant 10/10 chemistry; slow accumulation of "with me, he seems…" moments drives desire.

items.q: What should you remember about **Stories beat traits**?
items.a: **Humans bond through shared narratives and** unique moments (lab aliquoting prowess, Say Anything party observation), not checkbox compatibility.

items.q: What should you remember about **Trust your taste**?
items.a: **When face-to-face, believe "she's hot but I'm not** feeling this" over consensus or app filters; online makes it easy to sort people into fighting groups.

items.q: What should you remember about **Ask deeper questions**?
items.a: **Fast Friends / 36 questions elicit** reciprocal self-disclosure; the rush of being truly heard beats hotness alone for many people.

items.q: What should you remember about **Actions > words long-term**?
items.a: **Partner consistency (coffee, bed-making) predicts** stability more than verbal cleverness; apps can't filter for action patterns.

items.q: What should you remember about **Couple friends, not couple therapy with friends**?
items.a: **Social support works via shared** activities (double dates), not asking friends to assess your relationship.

items.q: What should you remember about **Finances & age myths**?
items.a: **Partner income has tiny effects on satisfaction; women-education-higher-than-man** is not a divorce risk (since the 1990s); both sexes prefer slightly younger partners when actually dating.

items.q: What should you remember about **Protect the bond**?
items.a: **Feeling partner is uniquely irreplaceable + derogating** alternatives stabilizes monogamy; repeated secretive escalation with outsiders is the real infidelity risk, not fleeting attraction.

items.q: What should you remember about **Get off the sidelines**?
items.a: **Organize recurring group activities (beach volleyball Fridays,** cooking nights); young adults socialize less — technology pulls away from the architecture we evolved for.
